meta.title: Duties of drivers
meta.summary: You will learn which documents you must carry, what a driver must do when required by the police and after a road traffic accident, how to document an accident with no casualties, and what a driver is expressly prohibited from doing: driving while intoxicated, holding a phone in your hand, handing over the wheel and driving a faulty vehicle.

p: The driver of a motor vehicle must carry the following and hand them over for inspection when required by a police officer or a transport control officer ⟦19⟧:
list: a driving licence or a temporary licence issued in its place. You do not have to carry a licence issued in Kazakhstan if you have an identity document with you;
the vehicle registration certificate (except one issued in Kazakhstan) or a document confirming ownership of the vehicle;
the waybill, the document for the goods (consignment note) and other documents required by law, except those registered in the unified transport document management system.
lesson.tip: A licence issued in Kazakhstan can be left at home, but then you must have an identity document with you. Without one, driving without your licence is prohibited ⟦20⟧.

p: A vehicle in international traffic is allowed to drive in Kazakhstan if it has the following, issued in accordance with international treaties: a registration certificate (for the vehicle or trailer), a registration number, the distinguishing sign of the country of registration, an identification mark and a document confirming that it has passed a technical inspection ⟦21⟧.

list: The officer who has stopped your vehicle comes up to you without delay, explains the reason for stopping you and, at your request, shows you their official ID without handing it over. If a violation has been detected or recorded automatically, the officer shows you these materials (para. 7, version in force from 12.07.2026).

Stop when required to by a uniformed police officer or transport control officer. The signal is given through a loudspeaker, or by a hand gesture or a baton pointed at your vehicle, together with a whistle. The signal must be clear and given in good time ⟦22⟧.
If a police officer has stopped your vehicle, do not leave it without the officer's permission ⟦23⟧.
When required by a police officer, undergo an examination for intoxication ⟦24⟧.
In the cases established by the Code of Administrative Offences, a driver must take a test of their knowledge of the Rules ⟦25⟧.
Whenever you leave your vehicle, whatever the situation, take measures to prevent it from rolling away on its own ⟦26⟧.

lesson.h: Seat belts, motorcycle helmets and motorcycles
p: If the vehicle is fitted with seat belts, the driver must wear a seat belt and must not carry passengers who are not wearing seat belts ⟦27⟧. Passengers must also wear seat belts ⟦28⟧.

On a motorcycle or moped, the driver must wear a fastened motorcycle helmet and must not carry passengers who are not wearing a fastened motorcycle helmet ⟦29⟧. In addition, the driver of a motorcycle or moped is prohibited from:
list: riding without holding the handlebars with at least one hand ⟦30⟧;
riding on one wheel or being positioned anywhere other than the driving position ⟦31⟧;
carrying a load that projects more than 50 cm beyond the vehicle's dimensions in length or width, or that interferes with control ⟦32⟧.
lesson.tip: The driver is also responsible for a passenger who is not wearing a seat belt: carrying such a passenger is prohibited.

lesson.h: When you must provide your vehicle
p: A driver must provide the vehicle ⟦33⟧:
list: to a medical worker travelling in the same direction to provide medical assistance;
regardless of the direction of travel, to medical workers, police officers and officers of the national security bodies, to take a person in urgent need of medical assistance to a medical facility;
during counter-terrorist operations, with reimbursement of costs;

to police officers, to transport vehicles damaged in road traffic accidents or to get to the scene of a natural disaster; to officers of the police, the State Security Service and the national security bodies, in other cases provided for by law.
lesson.tip: Whoever has used your vehicle must, at your request, give you a certificate or make an entry in the waybill (trip duration, distance, surname, position, ID number, organisation), and their organisation reimburses the costs at the owner's request. Vehicles of missions with diplomatic immunity are exempt from this obligation.

lesson.h: If a road traffic accident happens
p: A driver involved in a road traffic accident must ⟦34⟧:
list: stop immediately and not move the vehicle, switch on the hazard warning lights and put out a warning triangle (or a flashing red lamp) as required by para. 45;
not move objects related to the accident;

give first aid to the casualties and call an ambulance. In an emergency, send the casualties in a passing vehicle or, if that is impossible, take them in your own vehicle to the nearest medical facility, give your surname and registration number there (showing your documents) and return to the scene of the accident;
report the accident immediately to the nearest police department, write down the names and addresses of eyewitnesses and wait for the police, except in the cases provided for in para. 8 of the Rules;

clear the carriageway if other vehicles cannot get past. Before doing so, record the position of the vehicle, the marks and the objects related to the accident in the presence of witnesses, take measures to preserve them and arrange for traffic to drive around the scene.
lesson.tip: The order: stop, hazard warning lights and warning triangle, help people, report to the police, wait. Do not move the vehicle except in three cases: others cannot get past (record everything in front of witnesses first), there is nobody but you to take a casualty to hospital, or you are documenting the accident under para. 8.

lesson.h: Accidents with no casualties: a diagram or simplified documentation
p: If nobody has been injured and the drivers agree in their assessment of what happened, they may draw up a diagram of the accident, sign it and go together to the nearest police station to have the accident documented ⟦35⟧.

Simplified documentation means completing the accident documents without any police officers at all, in the cases established by the Law on Compulsory Insurance of Civil Liability of Vehicle Owners ⟦36⟧. The main conditions: only two vehicles are involved in the accident, both drivers have an OGPO (compulsory civil liability insurance) policy, nobody has been injured and no harm has been caused to third parties, there is no dispute about the circumstances or who is at fault, and the damage does not exceed the set limit.
If the drivers disagree, the general rule applies: report to the police, write down the names and addresses of eyewitnesses and wait for the police at the scene ⟦37⟧.
lesson.tip: Do not touch debris or other objects related to the accident: their position is needed for documenting it.

list: You must not drive while intoxicated (by alcohol, drugs or toxic substances), under the influence of medicines that impair reaction and attention, or while ill or tired ⟦38⟧.

You must not hand over the wheel to a person who is intoxicated, under the influence of such medicines, ill or tired, or to someone who has no licence for that category, is not named in the waybill, has no right to drive or has been disqualified from driving. The exception is a learner driver during learner driving ⟦39⟧.

After an accident you are involved in, or after being stopped by the police, you must not consume alcohol, narcotic or psychotropic substances until you have undergone an examination for intoxication or an authorised person has decided to exempt you from it ⟦40⟧.
lesson.tip: “I had a drink after the crash to calm down” is a violation. Before the examination, not a single drop.

list: While driving, you may use a phone or a two-way radio only with headphones or a hands-free speaker ⟦41⟧.
You must not cut across organised convoys, including organised groups of pedestrians, or take a place in them ⟦42⟧.
You must not drive without state number plates or with number plates that do not match the registration documents ⟦43⟧.
You must not drive if, in the cases established by law, the vehicle owner has not taken out compulsory civil liability insurance ⟦44⟧.
You must not park in places equipped with electric vehicle charging stations unless you are charging your vehicle ⟦45⟧.

You must not drive a faulty vehicle or a vehicle that has not passed the compulsory technical inspection. The exception for the technical inspection: category M1 vehicles no more than 7 years old, including the year of manufacture, if they are not used for business activities in road transport ⟦46⟧.

It is prohibited to drive with an inoperative service braking system or steering, or with a faulty coupling device in a road train. During the hours of darkness on an unlit road, or in poor visibility, you must not drive with headlights or rear position lamps that are not lit. In rain or snowfall, you must not drive with faulty windscreen wipers ⟦47⟧.
Brakes or steering are considered inoperative if they do not allow you to stop or perform a manoeuvre even at minimum speed (note to para. 12(9)).

If other faults that prohibit the use of the vehicle occur on the way (for example, the horn stops working), the driver must fix them or, if that is impossible, drive to a parking place or a place of repair, taking precautions ⟦48⟧. With the faults listed in para. 12(9), you may not drive on in this way.
lesson.tip: Inoperative brakes or steering, a faulty road train coupling device, windscreen wipers not working in rain or snowfall, headlights or rear position lamps not lit at night on an unlit road or in poor visibility: with these you must not drive. With other faults, you may carefully make your way to a place of repair or parking.

keyFacts: You do not have to carry a licence issued in Kazakhstan if you have an identity document with you ⟦1⟧.
You do not have to carry a registration certificate issued in Kazakhstan ⟦2⟧.
A driver stopped by the police must not leave the vehicle without the officer's permission ⟦3⟧.
The driver must wear a seat belt and must not carry passengers who are not wearing one ⟦4⟧.
A phone while driving: only with headphones or a hands-free speaker ⟦5⟧.
In an accident: stop, switch on the hazard warning lights, put out a warning triangle and do not move any objects ⟦6⟧.
After an accident, clear the carriageway if others cannot get past, and only after recording everything in the presence of witnesses ⟦7⟧.
After an accident or being stopped by the police: no alcohol until the examination for intoxication or a decision to exempt you from it ⟦8⟧.

Driving without the compulsory technical inspection is prohibited. The exception is an M1 vehicle no more than 7 years old, including the year of manufacture, if it is not used for business activities in road transport ⟦9⟧.
Inoperative brakes or steering are those that do not allow you to stop or perform a manoeuvre at minimum speed ⟦10⟧.
Parking at an electric vehicle charging station without charging is prohibited ⟦11⟧.
A driver must provide the vehicle to a medical worker travelling in the same direction to give medical assistance ⟦12⟧.
mistakes: “I'll just have a quick chat with the phone in my hand”. Not allowed: only with headphones or a hands-free speaker ⟦13⟧.
“The passenger is an adult, let them decide whether to wear a seat belt”. The driver must not carry passengers who are not wearing seat belts ⟦14⟧.

Moving the car away immediately after an accident “so as not to get in the way”. First the hazard warning lights and the warning triangle; you may move the car only if others cannot get past, and after recording everything in the presence of witnesses ⟦15⟧.
Having a drink after an accident “to calm down”. This is prohibited until the examination for intoxication or a decision to exempt you from it ⟦16⟧.
Thinking that you may never drive without your licence on you. You do not have to carry a licence issued in Kazakhstan if you have an identity document ⟦17⟧.
Letting a friend who has “only had a little to drink” drive. Handing over control of the vehicle to an intoxicated person is prohibited ⟦18⟧.

questions.q: A police officer has stopped you. You have left your driving licence, issued in Kazakhstan, at home, but you have your identity card with you. Have you broken the rule on carrying documents?
options: Yes, you must always carry your licence
No, this is allowed with a Kazakhstani licence
No, if you can give the licence number from memory
Yes, if you are driving someone else's car, not your own
questions.explain: A driver must carry a driving licence, except for a licence issued in Kazakhstan when the driver has an identity document with them.

questions.q: A uniformed police officer has pointed a baton at your car and at the same time blown a whistle. What must you do?
options: Carry on driving if you have not broken any rules
Stop only if the officer is at a fixed police post
Stop your vehicle
Stop only after the signal is repeated
questions.explain: A driver must stop when required to by a uniformed police officer by means of a gesture or a baton pointed at the vehicle, together with a whistle.

questions.q: A police officer has stopped your car and walked back to the patrol car. You need to go to the shop opposite. May you get out and go?
options: No, not without the police officer's permission
Yes, if you switch off the engine and apply the parking brake
Yes, if you leave your documents on the dashboard
Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights
questions.explain: A driver must not leave a vehicle stopped by a police officer without that officer's permission.

questions.q: All the seats in the car have seat belts. You are wearing yours, but a passenger in the back refuses to fasten their seat belt. What should you do?
options: Drive off: the passenger is responsible for themselves
Do not drive until they fasten their seat belt
Drive, but only in town
Drive if the passenger is sitting in the middle
questions.explain: The driver of a vehicle fitted with seat belts must wear a seat belt and must not carry passengers who are not wearing seat belts.

questions.q: How do the Rules allow you to talk on the phone while driving?
options: Holding the phone in your hand, if the call is short
Holding the phone in your hand, but only at low speed
Not at all: phones are completely banned while driving
With headphones or a hands-free speaker
questions.explain: While driving, you must not use a phone or a two-way radio, except with headphones or a hands-free speaker.

questions.q: You have taken a medicine whose leaflet says that it slows reactions and reduces attention. May you drive?
options: Yes, it is not alcohol, after all
Yes, if you drive slowly in the daytime
No, not while the medicine is working
questions.explain: Driving a vehicle under the influence of medicines that impair reaction and attention is prohibited.

questions.q: Your friend has had a glass of wine and asks to drive your car home. He has a driving licence. What should you do?
options: Let him, if you sit next to him
Let him, if it is not far
Refuse, even after just one glass
Let him, if he has long driving experience
questions.explain: A driver must not hand over control of the vehicle to a person who is intoxicated, whether or not that person has a driving licence.

questions.q: You have been involved in a road traffic accident. What must you do first?
options: Move the car onto the shoulder so that it does not obstruct others
Stop, turn on the hazard warning lights, put out a warning triangle
Drive away if the damage is very minor
First clear all the debris off the road
questions.explain: A driver involved in an accident must stop immediately, not move the vehicle, switch on the hazard warning lights, put out a warning triangle and not move objects related to the accident.

questions.q: A pedestrian has been injured in an accident. You have called an ambulance, but help is needed urgently and there are no passing vehicles. What do the Rules require you to do?
options: Wait for the ambulance without doing anything else
Take the casualty to hospital yourself, then go about your own business
Ask passers-by to carry the casualty further away from the road
Take them to hospital, give your name and car registration, come back
questions.explain: In an emergency, casualties are sent in a passing vehicle; if that is impossible, you take them yourself, give your details there and return to the scene of the accident.

questions.q: After an accident, the cars are blocking the road. In the presence of witnesses, you have recorded the position of the cars, the marks and the debris, and cleared the carriageway. What else do the Rules require you to do?
options: Preserve the marks and let traffic get round the scene
Nothing: after recording everything, you can all go home
Sweep all the debris and skid marks off the road
Call your insurance company and wait for its representative
questions.explain: When clearing the carriageway, the driver records the position of the vehicles, marks and objects in the presence of witnesses, takes all possible measures to preserve them and arranges for traffic to drive around the scene. You must not leave: next you must report to the police and wait for officers, except in the cases covered by para. 8.

questions.q: You have been involved in an accident and are very shaken. May you drink a little alcohol before the police arrive, since you are not driving anywhere now?
options: Yes, since the car is not moving
No
Yes, if the other driver does not object
Yes, if nobody was injured in the accident
questions.explain: After an accident in which you are involved, you must not drink alcohol until you have undergone an examination for intoxication or an authorised person has decided to exempt you from it.

questions.q: It is raining heavily, and your windscreen wiper has stopped working. What should you do?
options: Carry on driving with the hazard warning lights on
Carry on driving if the windscreen demister works
Stop driving
Drive on, but no faster than the traffic flow
questions.explain: It is raining and the windscreen wiper is not working: driving with this fault from para. 12(9) is prohibited, so you must stop. The rule in para. 11 about driving to a place of repair applies only to other faults.

questions.q: A medical worker who is going your way to see a patient asks you for a lift so that they can give medical help. What should you do?
options: You may refuse: it is your private car
It is enough to call them a taxi
You must help only if a police officer asks
You must provide them with your vehicle
questions.explain: A driver must provide the vehicle to a medical worker travelling in the same direction to provide medical assistance.

questions.q: You want to leave your petrol car for half an hour in a space equipped with an electric vehicle charging station. Is this allowed?
options: No, unless you are charging the car
Yes, if there are no electric cars nearby
Yes, if you switch on the hazard warning lights
Yes, if you stay in the car
questions.explain: A driver must not park in places equipped with electric vehicle charging stations without charging.

questions.q: The registration certificate for your car was issued in Kazakhstan. Must you carry it with you?
options: Yes, you may not drive without it in any circumstances
Only when travelling outside your own town
No, you need not carry one issued in Kazakhstan
Only if you are driving someone else's car
questions.explain: A driver must carry the vehicle registration certificate or a document confirming ownership, but a certificate issued in Kazakhstan is an exception.

questions.q: You are carrying goods in a truck. The consignment note is registered in the unified transport document management system. Do you need to carry a paper copy?
options: Yes, a paper consignment note is always required
Yes, if the load is heavier than 3.5 t
Only when carrying goods abroad
No, as it is in the unified system
questions.explain: A driver must have the waybill, the document for the goods and other documents for the vehicle, except those registered in the unified transport document management system.

questions.q: A patrol car is driving behind you, and a police officer is telling you through a loudspeaker to stop. What should you do?
options: Stop: this is a lawful way to require you to stop
Do not stop: a stop may only be required with a baton
Stop only if the patrol car overtakes you
Speed up so as not to get in its way
questions.explain: A uniformed police officer may require you to stop through a loudspeaker, or by a hand gesture or a baton pointed at the vehicle, together with a whistle. Stop in a safe place at the edge of the carriageway.

questions.q: What must a police officer who has stopped your car do?
options: Check your documents first; the reason need not be explained
Come up, explain the reason and show their ID on request
Hand you their official ID so that you can check it
Wait for you to come to the patrol car yourself
questions.explain: Persons entitled to check a driver's documents, on stopping a vehicle, come up to it without delay, explain the reason for stopping it and, at the driver's request, show their official ID for inspection without handing it over to the driver.

questions.q: You have been stopped for a violation that was recorded automatically by a special device. What must the officer present to you for review?
options: Materials confirming the recorded violation
Nothing: a verbal explanation is enough
Only the article number in the Code of Administrative Offences
Written permission from their superior to stop you
questions.explain: If a violation has been detected or recorded automatically, the officer who stops you presents the relevant materials to you for review. This is the wording of para. 7 in force from 12.07.2026.

questions.q: You have stopped on the shoulder of a steep descent and want to leave the car for a short while. What must you do?
options: Nothing, if you are away for less than 5 minutes
Only switch on the hazard warning lights
Take measures to stop the car rolling away
Leave the engine running at idle
questions.explain: A driver must not leave the vehicle without taking measures to prevent it from moving on its own: for example, apply the parking brake and engage a gear. On a descent, this is especially important.

questions.q: A police officer has stopped you and requires you to undergo an examination for intoxication. You are sure you are sober. What should you do?
options: Refuse, since you are sure you are sober
Agree only if you have been in an accident
Undergo it only if there are witnesses nearby
Undergo the examination
questions.explain: The driver of a motor vehicle must undergo an examination for intoxication when required by a police officer, even if the driver is sure they are sober.

questions.q: A police officer has stopped you and gone back to the patrol car to do the paperwork. May you drink a bottle of beer in the meantime, since you are not driving anywhere?
options: Yes: the car is stationary and you are not driving it now
No
Yes, if a sober passenger will drive the car afterwards
Yes, if more than 15 minutes have passed since you were stopped
questions.explain: After being stopped at the request of a police officer, a driver must not consume alcohol, narcotic or psychotropic substances until the examination for intoxication or until an authorised person decides to exempt the driver from it.

questions.q: When must a driver take a test of their knowledge of the Road Traffic Rules?
options: In cases set by the Code of Administrative Offences
Every year, at the vehicle's technical inspection
Only each time the driving licence is replaced
Only after an accident in which people were injured
questions.explain: A driver takes a test of their knowledge of the Rules in the cases established by the Code of Administrative Offences of the Republic of Kazakhstan.

questions.q: A police officer asks you to urgently take a person who needs medical assistance to hospital. The hospital is in the opposite direction to your route. What should you do?
options: You may refuse, as you are going the other way
You must, but only if the hospital is on your way
You must provide your vehicle
It is enough to call a taxi at your own expense
questions.explain: To take a person in urgent need of medical assistance to a medical facility, a driver provides the vehicle to medical workers, police officers and officers of the national security bodies, regardless of the driver's own direction of travel.

questions.q: For what purpose must a driver provide the vehicle to police officers?
options: To go to lunch or on personal errands
To carry the officer's personal belongings
None: you need not lend a private car
To get to the scene of a natural disaster
questions.explain: A driver provides the vehicle to police officers to transport vehicles damaged in accidents, to get to the scene of a natural disaster and in other cases provided for by law.

questions.q: Which vehicles are not covered by the requirement to provide a vehicle to officers and medical workers?
options: Vehicles of missions with diplomatic immunity
Taxis and any other vehicles with passengers inside
Cars over 10 years old and motorcycles
Any private cars that are not used as taxis
questions.explain: The requirement to provide a vehicle does not apply to vehicles of missions of foreign states and international organisations that have diplomatic immunity.

questions.q: An officer has used your car in a case provided for by the Rules. What must the officer do at your request?
options: Nothing: services to the state are provided free
Give a certificate or make an entry in the waybill
Pay you in cash for the trip straight away
Leave their official ID with you as a deposit
questions.explain: At the driver's request, whoever has used the vehicle gives a certificate or makes an entry in the waybill showing the duration of the trip, the distance travelled, their surname, position, official ID number and the name of their organisation.

questions.q: You have provided your car to officers of a state organisation in a case provided for by the Rules. Who reimburses your costs?
options: Nobody: providing the car is your duty
Your insurance company, under your OGPO policy
The officers' organisation, if you request it
The casualty who was carried in your car
questions.explain: The costs of providing the vehicle are reimbursed, at the owner's request, by the organisations whose officers used it.

questions.q: In what order does a driver act after an accident in which someone was injured?
options: Call the police - move the car to the shoulder - help the casualties
Help the casualties - move the car away - put out the warning triangle
Call a tow truck - phone the insurance company - help the casualties
Hazard warning lights, triangle - first aid, ambulance - call the police
questions.explain: First, the driver stops, does not move the vehicle, switches on the hazard warning lights and puts out a warning triangle. Then the driver helps the casualties and calls an ambulance, reports the accident to the police, writes down the details of eyewitnesses and waits for the police.

questions.q: You have had an accident in town, switched on the hazard warning lights and put out a warning triangle as shown in the diagram. Have you done the right thing?
options: Yes, everything is correct
No, the triangle is too close
No, the triangle goes in front of the car, not behind
No, with the hazard warning lights on, no triangle is needed
questions.explain: The triangle is only 10 m from the car. After an accident, it is placed on the side of greatest danger so as to warn other drivers in good time, but no closer than 15 m in a built-up area and 30 m outside one.

questions.q: You have had an accident out of town, switched on the hazard warning lights and put out a warning triangle as shown in the diagram. Have you done the right thing?
options: Yes, the distance is sufficient
No, out of town it must be at least 50 m away
No, the triangle goes right next to the car
No, a triangle is only put out at night
questions.explain: The triangle is behind the car, on the side of approaching vehicles, 30 m away. Outside a built-up area, this is the minimum distance. If the view is poor, the triangle is placed further away so that drivers notice the danger in time.

questions.q: After an accident with no casualties, your cars are in the right lane, and other vehicles are driving around them in the left lane without difficulty. You are waiting for the police. Do you need to clear the carriageway?
options: Yes, move the cars to the roadside at once
Yes, if the wait lasts more than 5 minutes
No, other vehicles can get past
Yes, but photograph the damage first
questions.explain: Other vehicles can get past here, so the cars are not moved until the police arrive. You need to clear the carriageway only if other vehicles cannot get through.

questions.q: After an accident, your car and the blue car are blocking both lanes of a narrow road, and other vehicles cannot get past. Nobody is injured. What should you do?
options: Touch nothing until the police arrive, even if it causes a jam
Move the cars to the shoulder at once without recording anything
Record everything in front of witnesses and clear the road
Leave the scene so as not to cause a traffic jam
questions.explain: Here other vehicles cannot get through, so the carriageway must be cleared. Before that, you record the position of the vehicles, the marks and the objects in the presence of witnesses, take measures to preserve them and arrange for traffic to drive around the scene.

questions.q: After an accident, pieces of broken headlights and part of a bumper are lying on the road. They do not prevent other vehicles from getting past. May you remove them before the police arrive?
options: Yes, debris on the road is dangerous for others
Yes, if you photograph them first
Yes, if the other driver does not mind
No, they must not be moved
questions.explain: A driver involved in an accident must not move objects related to it: their position matters for documenting the accident. Anything may be moved only if the carriageway has to be cleared, and only after recording everything in the presence of witnesses.

questions.q: You have reported the accident to the police. People who saw the collision are standing nearby. What else must you do?
options: Write down the eyewitnesses' details and wait for the police
Nothing: the police will deal with everything
Ask the eyewitnesses to leave so that they are not in the way
Photograph the eyewitnesses and then leave on your business
questions.explain: A driver involved in an accident reports it to the police, writes down the names and addresses of eyewitnesses and waits for the police, except in the cases provided for in para. 8 of the Rules.

questions.q: After an accident, nobody is injured, and you and the other driver agree about what happened. Under para. 8 of the Rules, how can you document the accident without waiting for the police at the scene?
options: Go your separate ways without any paperwork, as you both agree
Draw up a diagram, sign it and go to the police
Report the accident by phone and go home
Have everything documented by the nearest notary using a diagram
questions.explain: Nobody is injured, and the drivers agree in their assessment of what happened. In that case they may draw up a diagram, sign it and go to the nearest police station to have the accident documented. If the conditions for simplified documentation are met, you can even do without the police.

questions.q: After an accident, nobody is injured, but you and the other driver disagree about who is at fault. What should you do?
options: Draw up a diagram and go to the nearest police station
Document the accident the simplified way, via an app
Report to the police and wait at the scene
Go your separate ways and settle the dispute in court later
questions.explain: A diagram followed by a trip to the police, and simplified documentation, are possible only if the drivers agree in their assessment of what happened. There is no agreement, so the general rule applies: report to the police, write down the eyewitnesses' details and wait for the police.

questions.q: What do the Rules call simplified documentation of a road traffic accident?
options: Documenting it by phone with the police duty officer, with no visit to the scene
Documenting any accident in which nobody was injured
Documenting an accident at a notary's, without the insurer
Documenting it without the police, in cases set by the OGPO Law
questions.explain: Simplified documentation of an accident means completing the accident documents without police officers. The Law on Compulsory Insurance of Civil Liability of Vehicle Owners determines when it is possible.

questions.q: Three cars have collided in a chain. Nobody is injured, all the drivers have OGPO (compulsory civil liability insurance) policies, and there is no dispute about who is at fault. Can the accident be documented the simplified way, without the police?
options: Yes, all the conditions are met
No, there are more than two vehicles
Yes, if each driver's damage is small
No, this is only for accidents out of town
questions.explain: Simplified documentation is possible only in the cases established by the OGPO Law, and one of the conditions is that only two vehicles are involved in the accident. With three cars, the usual rules apply: report to the police and wait for officers, or act under para. 8.
questions.ref: para. 2(68); para. 8; Law on Compulsory Insurance of Civil Liability of Vehicle Owners

questions.q: Who on a motorcycle must wear a fastened motorcycle helmet?
options: Only the driver
Only the passenger
Both driver and passenger
No one, if the trip is short
questions.explain: When driving a motorcycle or moped, the driver must wear a fastened motorcycle helmet and must not carry passengers without a fastened motorcycle helmet.

questions.q: Which of the following do the Rules expressly prohibit for the driver of a motorcycle?
options: Holding the handlebars with one hand while giving a hand signal
Riding in the daytime with dipped headlights on
Carrying a passenger wearing a fastened motorcycle helmet
Riding on one wheel
questions.explain: It is prohibited to ride a motorcycle or moped on one wheel or to be positioned anywhere other than the driving position. You must hold the handlebars with at least one hand, so giving a hand signal is allowed.

questions.q: On a smooth road, a motorcyclist took both hands off the handlebars to adjust his jacket. Did he break the Rules?
options: Yes, he did
No, if the road is straight
No, if his speed is below 20 km/h
Yes, but only in a built-up area
questions.explain: A driver must not ride a motorcycle or moped without holding the handlebars with at least one hand.

questions.q: You are carrying planks on a moped that project 60 cm beyond its overall length. They do not interfere with control. May you ride like this?
options: Yes, as they do not interfere with control
Yes, if you tie a red flag to the planks
No, more than 50 cm is not allowed
No: loads may not be carried on a moped at all
questions.explain: On motorcycles and mopeds, it is prohibited to carry a load that projects more than 50 cm beyond the vehicle's dimensions in length or width, or a load that interferes with control. 60 cm is more than allowed.

questions.q: You are carrying planks on a moped that project 40 cm beyond its overall length. They do not interfere with control. May you ride like this?
options: Yes, up to 50 cm is allowed
No, any projecting load on a moped is prohibited
Yes, but only in daylight hours
No, no more than 30 cm is allowed
questions.explain: The ban applies to a load that projects more than 50 cm beyond the moped's dimensions in length or width, or that interferes with control. The load projects 40 cm and does not interfere with control, so you may ride like this, with the load securely fastened.

questions.q: Which of these signs or documents do the Rules expressly require a vehicle in international traffic to have in order to drive in Kazakhstan?
options: Kazakhstani state registration number plates
A vehicle registration certificate issued in Kazakhstan
A technical inspection passed only in Kazakhstan
The distinguishing sign of the country of registration
questions.explain: A vehicle in international traffic is allowed to drive if it has the following, issued in accordance with international treaties: a registration certificate (for the vehicle or trailer), a registration number, the distinguishing sign of the country of registration, an identification mark and a document confirming a technical inspection. Kazakhstani documents and number plates are not needed for this.

questions.q: On the way, your horn has stopped working, and you cannot fix the fault on the spot. What should you do?
options: Continue your journey along the route as usual
Drive carefully to a place of parking or repair
You must not drive at all; call a tow truck
Drive to the end of the route with the hazard warning lights on
questions.explain: A horn that does not work is a fault that prohibits use of the vehicle, but it is not on the special list in para. 12(9) (brakes, steering, coupling device, headlights in the dark, wipers in rain). With such “other” faults, a driver who cannot fix them drives to a place of parking or repair, taking precautions.

questions.q: A driver has a licence issued in another country. He has left it at his hotel, but he has his passport with him. May he drive a car?
options: Yes, his passport is enough for this
Yes, if he states his licence number
No, he may not
Yes, but only in daylight hours
questions.explain: Driving without a driving licence on you is prohibited. The only exception is for a licence issued in Kazakhstan, when the driver has an identity document.

questions.q: You have not slept for almost 24 hours and feel very tired. You need to go somewhere urgently. May you drive?
options: Yes, if you drink some coffee
Yes, if you drive slowly
Yes, if you turn the music up loud
No, not in this state
questions.explain: The Rules prohibit driving a vehicle while ill or tired to a degree that endangers road safety. Coffee and music do not relieve fatigue.

questions.q: Which types of intoxication are expressly named in the ban on driving a vehicle?
options: Alcohol, drug and toxic-substance intoxication
Only alcohol intoxication, if over the limit
Alcohol and drug, but not toxic-substance intoxication
The Rules do not specify the type of intoxication
questions.explain: It is prohibited to drive a vehicle in a state of alcohol, drug and (or) toxic-substance intoxication, or under the influence of medicines that impair reaction and attention.

questions.q: Your passenger car is 4 years old, including the year of manufacture. You use it only for personal purposes. Does it need to pass the compulsory technical inspection for you to drive it?
options: Yes, all vehicles need a technical inspection
No, such a car is exempt
Yes, if you drive out of town
No, the inspection has been abolished for all vehicles
questions.explain: Driving a vehicle without the compulsory technical inspection is prohibited, except for category M1 vehicles no more than 7 years old, including the year of manufacture, if they are not used for business activities in road transport. Your car falls under this exception.

questions.q: Your passenger car is 4 years old, including the year of manufacture, and you use it as a taxi. Does it need to pass the compulsory technical inspection?
options: No, cars under 7 years old do not need one
Yes, there is no exception for taxis
No, if the car carries no more than 4 passengers
Yes, but only once every 5 years
questions.explain: The exemption from the technical inspection applies only to category M1 vehicles no more than 7 years old that are not used for business activities in road transport. Running a taxi is exactly such an activity.

questions.q: May you drive a car if its owner has not taken out compulsory civil liability insurance (OGPO)?
options: Yes, if the driver is named in a power of attorney
Yes, but only in your own town
Yes, if the car is new
No
questions.explain: A driver must not drive a vehicle whose owner, in the cases established by law, has not taken out compulsory civil liability insurance for vehicle owners.

questions.q: May you drive a car if its state number plates do not match the registration documents?
options: Yes, if the plates are clean and legible
Yes, until the next technical inspection
No
Yes, if the plates are from another car of yours
questions.explain: It is prohibited to drive a vehicle without state registration number plates or with plates that do not match the registration documents.

questions.q: Your friend has a driving licence for category A only. He asks to drive your passenger car. What should you do?
options: Let him, as he has a licence
Let him, if you sit next to him
Let him, if he only drives in the yard
Refuse: category B is needed
questions.explain: A driver must not hand over control of the vehicle to someone who has no driving licence for that category of vehicle. A category A licence does not entitle you to drive a passenger car.

questions.q: To whom may a driver hand over control of the vehicle even though that person has no driving licence?
options: A learner driver during learner driving
A person disqualified from driving, if sober
A foreigner who has left their licence at the hotel
Nobody, under any circumstances
questions.explain: The ban on handing over control to a person without a driving licence does not apply to learner drivers. Learner driving on roads takes place only with a driving instructor, who is treated as the driver. You must not hand over the wheel to a person who has been disqualified from driving.

questions.q: An organised convoy escorted by a police car with its flashing beacons on is passing through an intersection. There are gaps between the vehicles in the convoy. May you drive through the intersection in a gap in the convoy?
options: Yes, if the gap between the vehicles is big enough
Yes, if you are on the main road
No, you must let the convoy pass
Yes, after sounding the horn in advance
questions.explain: You must let the entire convoy pass. A driver must not cut across organised convoys, including organised groups of pedestrians, or take a place in them.

questions.q: A taxi driver is answering the dispatcher on a two-way radio, holding the microphone in his hand while driving. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, the ban applies only to using mobile phones
No, only with headphones or a hands-free speaker
Yes, if the conversation is very short
Yes, if the speed is below 40 km/h
questions.explain: While driving a vehicle, it is prohibited to use a phone or a two-way radio, except with headphones or a hands-free speaker.

questions.q: Which service braking system is considered inoperative?
options: One whose warning lamp is lit on the dashboard
One whose braking distance on a dry road is slightly above the norm
One whose brake pads squeal loudly when braking
One that cannot stop the car even at minimum speed
questions.explain: A service braking system or steering is considered inoperative if it does not allow you to stop the vehicle or perform a manoeuvre when moving at minimum speed. Driving with such a fault is prohibited.

questions.q: At night on an unlit country road, both your headlights have gone out. You have stopped on the shoulder. May you carry on to the nearest garage?
options: No, driving in these conditions is prohibited
Yes, with the hazard warning lights on
Yes, if you drive slowly along the shoulder
Yes, as far as the nearest built-up area
questions.explain: During the hours of darkness on roads without artificial lighting, or in poor visibility, it is prohibited to drive with headlights or rear position lamps that are not lit. This is not one of the “other” faults under para. 11, so you may not drive to the garage under your own power.

questions.q: On the way, you notice that the coupling device between the towing vehicle and the trailer is faulty. May you drive to a workshop under your own power?
options: Yes, as long as you take precautions
Yes, if you drive no faster than 20 km/h
No, driving it there is prohibited
Yes, but only in daylight hours
questions.explain: A faulty coupling device in a road train is on the special list in para. 12(9), together with brakes and steering. With such faults, you may not drive even to a place of repair.
